problem_statement: The paper frames portfolio management as choosing asset weights that minimize risk and maximize return, especially when the number of assets and constraints is large. It also says the task becomes computationally intensive and that portfolio optimization must handle large data and nonlinear constraints.
problem_statement_quotes: The VQE aims at finding the best allocation of the portfolio; the best weights that correspond to minimum risk and maximum return as predicted by the modern portfolio theory.

Portfolio management, but especially the asset allocation procedure, requires finding the most appropriate mix of investments that incurs low risk and generates high return – a task that becomes computationally intensive if the number of assets and constraints is large[1].

The study assesses the suitability and speed of VQE in solving matters involving portfolio management tasks such as handling vast data and nonlinear constraints which are hard to solve through other optimization methods.
classical_baseline: The paper treats classical mean-variance optimization as the main baseline, and also compares against the Black-Litterman model. It describes the classical approach as solving a quadratic programming problem with portfolio variance as the objective and expected return and weights as constraints.
classical_baseline_quotes: The classical approach will be developed on the mean variance model which aims at minimizing the portfolio risk at a certain level of return or vice versa.
This is done by solving a quadratic programming problem or using another type of problem in which the goal function is usually portfolio variance and constraints are expected return and weights.
We’ll also compare the performance of the VQE with other classical methods including the Black-Litterman model of portfolio selection.
classical_difficulty: The paper says classical methods may not efficiently solve large-scale portfolio problems, especially when the number of assets and constraints is large. It also says these problems are computationally intensive and that classical optimization has limitations in computational capability and time for large, complex portfolios.
classical_difficulty_quotes: Some of the methods include the basic mean variance optimization technique which have been widely used in the development of portfolio theory but may not efficiently solve large scale problem.

This is especially the case given current and emerging complex structures of financial markets which call for new approaches to match the rising data, volatility and intricacies of optimization problems.

Albeit solving such problems these classical optimization methods have some imperatives when it comes to computational capability and time especially when the assets portfolio dimensions or constraint structure is large and complex.
extraction_notes: Motivation is explicit in abstract and introduction; paper is strongly framed around portfolio optimization with classical benchmarking.
